name: Bibimbap
genericFact: Bibimbap means 'mixed rice', and the crispy bottom of a hot stone bowl (dolsot) is a prized bite.

swaps.tip: Use a half portion of rice (or mixed grains) and pile on more namul vegetables. Keep the egg and gochujang.
Go easy on the gochujang and soy-seasoned namul, and season the vegetables with sesame oil, garlic and a little salt instead.

name: Bulgogi
genericFact: Bulgogi marinades often use grated Asian pear, whose enzymes help tenderize the beef.

swaps.tip: Use low-sodium soy sauce, sweeten the marinade with grated Asian pear instead of extra sugar, and bulk up the pan with onion and mushrooms.

name: Kimchi Jjigae
genericFact: Kimchi jjigae is a classic way to use up very sour, well-fermented kimchi.

swaps.tip: Use a homemade anchovy-and-kelp stock instead of salted broth, and cut back on gochujang and fish sauce. The kimchi already seasons the stew.

name: Kimchi
genericFact: Kimchi is fermented, which gives it live cultures and much of its saltiness.

name: Korean Fried Chicken
genericFact: Korean fried chicken is often fried twice for an extra-crisp crust.

swaps.tip: Air-fry or oven-bake the chicken with a thin cornstarch coating on a hot rack to keep it crisp.
Use a lighter glaze of gochujang thinned with rice vinegar and a little honey instead of adding more soy sauce.

name: Japchae
genericFact: Japchae noodles are made from sweet potato starch.

name: Tteokbokki
genericFact: Tteokbokki's chewy rice cakes are cylinders of pounded rice simmered in spicy sauce.

swaps.tip: Use fewer rice cakes and add cabbage, fish cake and a boiled egg for volume.
Thin the sauce with anchovy stock and use less gochujang and soy sauce.

name: Samgyeopsal (Pork Belly)
genericFact: Samgyeopsal means 'three-layer meat', named for the stripes of fat and lean in pork belly.

swaps.tip: Choose leaner cuts like pork neck (moksal) or loin, trim visible fat, grill on a rack, and wrap in lettuce with plenty of vegetables.

name: Sundubu Jjigae
genericFact: Sundubu jjigae is built on extra-soft, unpressed tofu.

swaps.tip: Use a homemade anchovy stock, go lighter on the chili-paste seasoning, and salt only at the end, to taste.

name: Gimbap
genericFact: Gimbap looks like sushi, but the rice is seasoned with sesame oil rather than vinegar.

swaps.tip: Use less rice and more vegetables, egg and lean fillings. Brown or mixed-grain rice works well.
Season the rice lightly and choose fresh fillings over ham, imitation crab and pickled items.

name: Pad Thai
genericFact: Pad thai is said to have been popularized in the 1940s as part of a push to promote a national dish.

swaps.tip: Use 1 tbsp of oil with egg and shrimp or tofu, and finish with just a small spoon of crushed peanuts.
Use half the rice noodles and add bean sprouts, garlic chives and shredded cabbage.
Cut back on the fish sauce and let tamarind and lime provide the tang.

name: Green Curry with Chicken
genericFact: Green curry gets its color from fresh green chilies in the paste.

swaps.tip: Use light coconut milk, or half coconut milk and half stock, and add more vegetables like Thai eggplant and bamboo shoots.
Use less fish sauce and curry paste, and finish with lime juice and Thai basil.

name: Tom Yum Soup
genericFact: Tom yum's sour-spicy aroma comes from lemongrass, galangal and kaffir lime leaves.

swaps.tip: Use low-sodium stock and less fish sauce. Lime, lemongrass and galangal carry the flavor.

name: Massaman Curry
genericFact: Massaman curry shows Persian and Malay influence, with spices like cardamom and cinnamon.

swaps.tip: Use light coconut milk, trim the meat, and add extra potato and onion to fill out the curry.
Use less fish sauce and curry paste, and add tamarind for tang.

name: Som Tam (Papaya Salad)
genericFact: Som tam is pounded in a mortar so the chilies, lime and garlic bruise together.

name: Chicken Satay
genericFact: Satay skewers are marinated in turmeric and coconut milk before grilling.

name: Mango Sticky Rice
genericFact: Sticky rice is steamed, then soaked in sweetened coconut milk.

swaps.tip: Use a smaller portion of sticky rice and more fresh mango.
Sweeten the coconut sauce lightly and let ripe mango do most of the work.

name: Pad Kra Pao with Rice
genericFact: Pad kra pao uses holy basil, which tastes peppery, different from Thai or Italian basil.

swaps.tip: Serve with a smaller scoop of jasmine rice and add long beans or green beans to the stir-fry.
Use less oyster, soy and fish sauce. Holy basil and fresh chilies give the flavor.

name: Thai Fried Rice
genericFact: Thai fried rice is typically seasoned with fish sauce and served with lime and cucumber.

swaps.tip: Use half the rice and double the egg, tomato and vegetables.
Cut the soy and fish sauce and squeeze in lime at the end for brightness.

name: Tom Kha Gai
genericFact: Tom kha gai's creaminess comes from coconut milk, balanced with galangal and lime.

swaps.tip: Use light coconut milk with extra mushrooms, or thin the soup with stock.
Use low-sodium stock and less fish sauce, and finish with lime.

name: Fresh Spring Rolls
genericFact: Fresh spring rolls aren't fried, so they are much lighter than the fried version.

name: Pho Bo (Beef Pho)
genericFact: Pho broth is simmered for hours with charred onion and ginger plus spices like star anise.

swaps.tip: Eat about half the noodles and add extra bean sprouts, herbs and sliced beef.
Drink only some of the broth, and flavor with lime, basil and jalapeño instead of hoisin and sriracha.

name: Banh Mi
genericFact: Banh mi blends Vietnamese ingredients with the French baguette.

swaps.tip: Use less pâté and mayo, and fill with grilled chicken or tofu plus extra pickled carrot, daikon and cucumber.
Go light on the pâté, cured cold cuts and soy-based seasoning. Pickled vegetables and cilantro add plenty of flavor.

name: Summer Rolls (Goi Cuon)
genericFact: Summer rolls wrap shrimp, herbs and rice noodles in rice paper without any frying.

name: Bun Cha
genericFact: Bun cha is a Hanoi specialty of grilled pork served with noodles and fresh herbs.

swaps.tip: Use leaner pork shoulder, trimmed, and grill it rather than pan-frying.
Use half the vermicelli and add extra lettuce and herbs.
Make the nuoc cham dipping sauce with less fish sauce and more lime juice and water.

name: Com Tam (Broken Rice with Pork)
genericFact: Com tam is made from broken rice grains, once considered a cheap leftover.

swaps.tip: Trim the fat from the grilled pork chop and skip fried toppings like scallion oil.
Serve a smaller portion of broken rice with extra cucumber and tomato.
Use less fish sauce in the marinade and the dressing.

name: Pho Ga (Chicken Pho)
genericFact: Chicken pho has a lighter, cleaner broth than beef pho.

swaps.tip: Drink only some of the broth, and add lime, basil and chili instead of extra hoisin or fish sauce.

name: Banh Xeo
genericFact: 'Banh xeo' means sizzling cake, named for the sound of batter hitting the hot pan.

swaps.tip: Use less oil in the pan and fill with more bean sprouts, shrimp and herbs, then wrap in lettuce.

name: Bo Luc Lac (Shaking Beef)
genericFact: Bo luc lac means 'shaking beef', for the way the cubes are shaken in the hot pan.

swaps.tip: Use lean sirloin, trimmed, with a tablespoon of oil in a very hot pan.
Use less soy and oyster sauce, and finish with lime juice and black pepper.

name: Che (Sweet Dessert Soup)
genericFact: Che is a family of Vietnamese sweet soups and puddings made with beans, fruit and coconut milk.

swaps.tip: Use less sugar in the syrup and rely on coconut milk, fruit and beans for sweetness.

name: Vietnamese Iced Coffee
genericFact: Vietnamese iced coffee uses sweetened condensed milk, a legacy of limited access to fresh milk.

swaps.tip: Use half the sweetened condensed milk, or a spoonful of it with a splash of regular milk.

name: Cha Gio (Fried Spring Rolls)
genericFact: Cha gio are fried rolls filled with pork, shrimp and vegetables.

swaps.tip: Bake or air-fry the rolls, or serve them fresh (goi cuon style) with the same herbs.

name: Doro Wat
genericFact: Doro wat is a slow-cooked chicken stew with berbere and a boiled egg, often called Ethiopia's national dish.

swaps.tip: Use skinless chicken and cook the onion base with less niter kibbeh (spiced butter). The berbere carries the flavor.
Salt the stew at the end, to taste, and make your own berbere blend to control the salt.

name: Injera
genericFact: Injera is a fermented flatbread made from teff, a tiny, iron-rich grain.

name: Misir Wot (Red Lentil Stew)
genericFact: Red lentils cook quickly into a thick, spicy stew with berbere.

name: Shiro Wot
genericFact: Shiro is a stew made from ground chickpea or broad bean flour, popular on fasting days.

name: Kitfo
genericFact: Kitfo is minced beef seasoned with mitmita spice and niter kibbeh, often served rare.

swaps.tip: Use lean sirloin and just a little niter kibbeh, and serve it with plenty of gomen and fresh ayib cheese.

name: Gomen (Collard Greens)
genericFact: Gomen is collard greens, a good source of vitamin C and calcium.

name: Beef Tibs
genericFact: Tibs are sautéed pieces of meat, often cooked with onion, peppers and rosemary.

swaps.tip: Choose lean beef, trim the fat, and sauté in a little oil or niter kibbeh with plenty of onion and pepper.

name: Ethiopian Combo Platter
genericFact: Combination platters pair several stews with injera and are meant to be shared.

swaps.tip: Choose more lentil and vegetable stews (misir, gomen, atkilt) and fewer oil-rich meat dishes.
Share the platter and use less injera, leaning on the stews and vegetables.
Ask for stews lightly salted and rely on berbere and mitmita for flavor.

name: Firfir
genericFact: Firfir is torn injera stirred into spicy sauce, a way to use up leftover bread.

swaps.tip: Use less torn injera and add more of the stew or vegetables.
Use less salt in the sauce and let berbere provide the heat and depth.

name: Atkilt Wat
genericFact: Atkilt wat is a mild stew of cabbage, carrots and potatoes.

name: Gyro
genericFact: Gyro meat is cooked on a vertical rotisserie and shaved into pita.

swaps.tip: Use grilled chicken or lean lamb sliced thin, and swap some tzatziki for extra tomato and cucumber.
Go lighter on the seasoned meat and feta. Tomatoes, onion and fresh herbs add flavor.

name: Chicken Souvlaki
genericFact: Souvlaki is skewered grilled meat, one of Greece's most common street foods.

name: Greek Salad
genericFact: A traditional Greek salad has no lettuce: tomato, cucumber, onion, olives and feta.

swaps.tip: Use 1 tbsp of olive oil and a smaller slab of feta, and add more cucumber, tomato and pepper.
Rinse the olives and capers, use less feta (it's salty), and season with oregano and lemon.

name: Spanakopita
genericFact: Spanakopita is spinach and feta baked in layers of phyllo.

swaps.tip: Brush the phyllo lightly with olive oil (or use a spray) and use fewer layers, with more spinach and herbs.

name: Moussaka
genericFact: Moussaka layers eggplant, spiced meat sauce and béchamel.

swaps.tip: Roast or grill the eggplant instead of frying it, use lean lamb or beef, and make a lighter béchamel with low-fat milk.
Rinse rather than heavily salt the eggplant, and use no-salt-added tomatoes.

name: Tzatziki
genericFact: Tzatziki is strained yogurt with cucumber, garlic and olive oil.

name: Dolmades
genericFact: Dolmades are grape leaves stuffed with rice and herbs.

name: Pastitsio
genericFact: Pastitsio is a baked pasta with meat sauce and béchamel, sometimes called Greek lasagna.

swaps.tip: Use lean beef or turkey and a lighter béchamel made with low-fat milk.
Use unsalted tomato sauce and less cheese (kefalotyri is salty).

name: Loukoumades
genericFact: Loukoumades are fried dough balls dipped in honey syrup, with a history that reaches back to ancient Greece.

swaps.tip: Bake or air-fry the puffs and drizzle a thin honey-cinnamon syrup instead of soaking them.

name: Avgolemono Soup
genericFact: Avgolemono is a lemon-egg soup that is thickened without cream.

swaps.tip: Use homemade or low-sodium chicken stock. The lemon and egg add flavor, not salt.

name: Greek Yogurt with Honey
genericFact: Strained Greek yogurt has far more protein than regular yogurt.

swaps.tip: Drizzle 1 tsp of honey instead of 2 tbsp, and add walnuts and fresh fruit.
